tools.description:
Query Automation Metrics

Query execution counts per bucket for one automation. Batches are bucketed by creation time and tasks by completion time; only succeeded tasks are counted. Reboot automations also report recovered hashrate and estimated 24-hour revenue.
tools.name: QueryAutomationMetrics

tools.description:
List Automation Tasks

List succeeded tasks dispatched by one automation in the time range, newest first. Each task carries its linked reboot snapshots and recovery when available.
tools.name: ListAutomationTasks

Search Miners

Search miners in the farm with structured filters.
tools.name: SearchMiners

tools.description:
Get Miner

Get a miner by ID.
tools.name: GetMiner

tools.description:
List Racks

Deprecated: racks are replaced by rack groups. Use `ListRackGroups` instead. This operation will be removed once it has no callers. List the racks of a farm with their size, allocation and miner counts, in natural name order. A rack exists without miners; search miners with `rack` to get its miners, or with `rack: null` for miners without a rack.
tools.name: ListRacks

tools.description:
List Miner Reboot Tasks

List reboot task history for a miner. Equivalent to ListMinerTasks with task_name=miner.system.reboot.
tools.name: ListMinerRebootTasks

tools.description:
List Miner Tasks

Return task execution history for a specific miner.
tools.name: ListMinerTasks

tools.description:
Query Miner Metrics

Query time-bucketed performance metrics for a single miner.
tools.name: QueryMinerMetrics

tools.description:
Query Farm Metrics

Query time-bucketed aggregate metrics for a farm.
tools.name: QueryFarmMetrics

tools.description:
Query Farm Hashrate Comparison Metrics

Query a precomputed pool hashrate comparison for a 7-day or 28-day UTC-aligned window and its previous window.
tools.name: QueryFarmHashrateComparisonMetrics

tools.description:
Query Farm Miner Metrics

Return real-time aggregate miner classification counts and mining-mode and model distributions for a farm. Each model and submodel includes its firmware distribution; unreported firmware is null. Classification counts are independent — a sleeping miner with a fault appears in both abnormal and sleep. Online miners equal total minus stale.
tools.name: QueryFarmMinerMetrics

tools.description:
Query Farm Account Metrics

Return the online miners of a farm grouped by the pool and account receiving their hashrate, with miner count and total hashrate. A miner's account is the worker name before the first `.` on the pool connection with the latest share; `active` is not used because a miner can stay connected to several pools. Use Search Miners with `pool` and `account` to retrieve the miners behind an entry.
tools.name: QueryFarmAccountMetrics

tools.description:
Query Farm Monitor Event Metrics

Aggregate farm monitor events using the same selection filters as SearchFarmMonitorEvents. Use status=active with alert_entered=true for the current alert overview, then SearchFarmMonitorEvents with the same filters for members. Counts describe events and distinct objects within each monitor type. Use current farm metrics to assess present health.
tools.name: QueryFarmMonitorEventMetrics

tools.description:
Search Farm Monitor Events

Search farm monitor events by shared selection filters, ordered by started_at and id. The default window is 24 hours, with a maximum of 7 days. Use status=active with both bounds omitted for all matching active events; add alert_entered=true for confirmed alert members. Use agent_id for miners currently managed by an agent, object_type=["farm","agent"] for the incident timeline, event_ids for exact event lookup, and detail=snapshot (max 100 per page) for frozen snapshots.
tools.name: SearchFarmMonitorEvents

tools.description:
List Rack Groups

List the rack groups of a farm in subnet order, each with its subnets, template, start offset and a real-time summary of its miners. Every /24 subnet with miners that no rack group covers gets a new unnamed rack group first, so the list covers every IPv4 miner of the farm. Search miners with `ip_ranges` set to a rack group's subnets to get its miners.
tools.name: ListRackGroups

tools.description:
Update Rack Groups

Name rack groups, set their template and start offset, or replace their subnets, in one transaction. Each change identifies a rack group by id; omitted fields keep their values. With a `sequential` template, slot 1 holds the miner at `start_offset` within the subnets, which is the last octet for a single /24. New subnets absorb every other rack group whose subnets all fall within them, deleting it with its name and template; a subnet that only partly overlaps another rack group is rejected. A /24 with miners left uncovered gets a new rack group on the next read.
tools.name: UpdateRackGroups

tools.description:
List Rack Group Templates

List the templates a farm can apply to its rack groups: read-only system templates shared by every farm, then the templates of the farm, each by name. A template sets the racks of a rack group, the rows and columns of each rack, and how miners take slots.
tools.name: ListRackGroupTemplates

tools.description:
Create Rack Group Template

Create a template for the farm, for rack group models that no system template describes. Names are unique within the farm. Apply the template to rack groups with UpdateRackGroups.
tools.name: CreateRackGroupTemplate

tools.description:
Update Rack Group Template

Change a template of the farm; omitted fields keep their values. Rack groups using the template follow the change. System templates are read-only; create a farm template instead.
tools.name: UpdateRackGroupTemplate

tools.description:
Delete Rack Group Template

Delete a template of the farm. Rack groups using it are left without a template. System templates are read-only.
tools.name: DeleteRackGroupTemplate

tools.description:
Get Farm Layout

Get the layout of a farm: rows from front to back, the rack groups stacked at each position from the floor up, and the aisle after each row. `rows` is null until someone arranges the farm. Rows may refer to rack groups deleted since; skip those. Pass `updated_at` as `expected_updated_at` when saving with UpdateFarmLayout.
tools.name: GetFarmLayout

tools.description:
Update Farm Layout

Replace the whole layout of a farm. Refer to rack groups by id from ListRackGroups; a rack group takes at most one position, and a position stacks at most two. Pass the `updated_at` read with GetFarmLayout as `expected_updated_at`, or null when no layout was saved; the save is rejected if the layout changed since.
tools.name: UpdateFarmLayout

tools.description:
List Farm Reboot Events

List detected Farm Reboot Events in the requested farm. Before averages use T-30 to T-5 minutes and after averages use T+15 to T+60 minutes. The default time range is the last 7 days and the maximum is 30 days.
tools.name: ListFarmRebootEvents

tools.description:
List Miner Reboot Events

List detected Miner Reboot Events for one Miner. Before averages use T-30 to T-5 minutes and after averages use T+15 to T+60 minutes. The default time range is the last 7 days and the maximum is 30 days.
tools.name: ListMinerRebootEvents

tools.description:
List Task Batches

List the task batches of a farm, newest first, to review the operations run on its miners and agents and whether they succeeded. Use SearchTaskBatches to filter by status, task type, creator or time. Keep queries small: filter as precisely as you can, use a small page_size, and fetch more pages only when needed.
tools.name: ListTaskBatches

tools.description:
Search Task Batches

Find task batches in a farm by status, task type, creator (user, automation or api) or creation time, for example batches that are still running or automation runs that failed. Set a creation time window whenever you can. Keep queries small: filter as precisely as you can, use a small page_size, and fetch more pages only when needed.
tools.name: SearchTaskBatches

tools.description:
Get Task Batch

Get the progress of one task batch: its parameters and how many of its tasks succeeded, failed or are still running. Use ListTaskBatchTasks to see which miners or agents failed and why.
tools.name: GetTaskBatch

tools.description:
List Task Batch Tasks

List the tasks of one task batch, one per miner or agent, with the result or error of each. Filter by status, for example failed, to find the miners that need attention, or use it to download collected logs. Keep queries small: filter as precisely as you can, use a small page_size, and fetch more pages only when needed.
tools.name: ListTaskBatchTasks

tools.description:
List Task Batch Recoveries

List succeeded tasks in one task batch with their linked reboot snapshots and recovery. Recovery is null when the task has no linked reboot event or hashprice data.
tools.name: ListTaskBatchRecoveries

tools.description:
Create Reboot Task Batch

Restart the specified miners, for example to recover miners that are stuck or underperforming. Miners stop hashing until they are back up. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateRebootTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Firmware Update Task Batch

Install the firmware at firmware_url on the specified miners. Miners reboot and stop hashing until the update completes. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateFirmwareUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Pool Lock Task Batch

Lock the specified miners to the pools set by the authentication package at auth_url, or unlock them so their pools can be changed again. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreatePoolLockTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Mining Mode Update Task Batch

Set the mining mode of the specified miners: sleep, low, normal or high, or a firmware preset name. Sleep stops hashing until another mode is set. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateMiningModeUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Light Update Task Batch

Turn the locator light of the specified miners on or off to find them on the rack. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateLightUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Log Collection Task Batch

Collect the current log of the specified miners to troubleshoot them. Download the logs from ListTaskBatchTasks. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateLogGetTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Tags Update Task Batch

Add or remove tags on the specified miners to group and filter them. The tags off_rack, transit, maintenance, retired and archived also mark an operational status that changes farm summaries.
tools.name: CreateTagsUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Network Update Task Batch

Set the address each of the specified miners answers on. The whole batch is rejected if any address is already used by another miner in the farm, because a miner that takes an address another one holds cannot be reached to correct it. An address outside the scanned ranges is allowed: the miner stays reachable there, and adding the range brings it back into view.
tools.name: CreateNetworkUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Record Delete Task Batch

Remove the specified miners from the miner list of the farm, for example after they are retired or moved. A miner still on the network comes back with the next agent report unless its address is removed from the scan ranges.
tools.name: CreateRecordDeleteTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Agent Scan Task Batch

Make the agents in the farm scan for miners in ip_ranges, or in the configured ranges of the farm when ip_ranges is omitted, to discover new or moved miners. Miners outside the scanned ranges stop being monitored, so pass every range unless you mean to drop the rest. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateAgentScanTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Agent IP Diagnosis Task Batch

Make the agents in the farm check which miner addresses are reachable, to troubleshoot miners that cannot be reached. Download the report from ListTaskBatchTasks. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateAgentIpDiagnosisTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Agent Self Update Task Batch

Update the agents in the farm to the signed agent build at binary_url. Agents restart and stop reporting miner data until they are back. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateAgentSelfUpdateTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Agent Pause Task Batch

Stop the agents in the farm from reporting miner data, for example during maintenance. While paused, the miners of the farm show as stale and miner tasks are rejected. Undo with CreateAgentResumeTaskBatch. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateAgentPauseTaskBatch

tools.description:
Create Agent Resume Task Batch

Make the paused agents in the farm report miner data again. Tasks run asynchronously on the agents in the farm; track them with GetTaskBatch.
tools.name: CreateAgentResumeTaskBatch

tools.description:
List Webhook Endpoints

List your webhook endpoints in the workspace with their delivery status.
tools.name: ListWebhookEndpoints

tools.description:
Create Webhook Endpoint

Send the chosen event types of the chosen farms to an HTTPS URL, for example only hashrate_drop.alert_entered. Alerts confirmed after creation are delivered. The response contains the signing secret, which is never returned again. Each alert is sent as a JSON POST signed with Standard Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature: v1,base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>" keyed by the base64-decoded part of the whsec_ secret). webhook-id stays the same across retries; use it to drop duplicates. A 2xx response is success; 408, 429, 5xx, and timeouts (10 seconds) are retried for about two hours with exponential backoff and jitter; other responses are not retried. An endpoint whose deliveries keep failing after all retries for 3 days is disabled and its owner is emailed.
tools.name: CreateWebhookEndpoint

tools.description:
Get Webhook Endpoint

Get one of your webhook endpoints. status, consecutive_failures, and last_failure_reason explain missing deliveries.
tools.name: GetWebhookEndpoint

tools.description:
Update Webhook Endpoint

Change the name, URL, event types, or farms of your webhook endpoint, or set enabled to stop or resume delivery. Fields left out keep their values. Newly added monitor types deliver alerts confirmed after the change.
tools.name: UpdateWebhookEndpoint

tools.description:
Delete Webhook Endpoint

Delete your webhook endpoint. Deliveries still waiting to be sent are cancelled.
tools.name: DeleteWebhookEndpoint
